Why site speed testing and mobile compatibility are important

In 2025, in the fast digital age we live in, a website is no longer just a virtual business card. It is the face of your business online, the showcase, the sales office, the support center, and sometimes also the place where potential customers meet you for the first time. Whether you run a small image site, Wide online store or a blog rich in content, it is very important that your website is proper, efficient, and provides an excellent user experience. All of these are keys to success in today's digital age.

One of the ways to ensure the success of the site is execution Website speed test comprehensive This is a thorough process, sometimes neglected, but one that can make all the difference between a site that leads to success and a site that falters.

In this article, we will examine the world of website testing in depth. We will talk about why it is so important, what is included in the process, how it affects Website promotion in search engines (SEO) and about the user experience (UX), and how tools like Google PageSpeed ​​Insights come into play and affect the whole process. Our goal is to provide you with all the information you will need to understand the importance of the test, and perhaps also encourage you to perform one yourself or with the help of skilled professionals. The article is intended for website owners, marketing managers, website promoters, and anyone interested in ensuring that their digital asset works optimally and achieves its goals effectively.

What is a website speed test and why is it so critical?

simply put, Website speed test It is a systematic process in which an analysis and evaluation of all the different aspects of your website is performed. The main goal is to identify problems, weaknesses and opportunities for improvement that can help the site perform better. This is an essential process that helps ensure that the website not only works properly, but also provides an excellent user experience and is focused on achieving its goals - whether it is to increase sales, attract more visitors or improve visibility in search engines.

You can imagine it like a periodic medical checkup for your car. You don't wait until the car gets stuck in the middle of the road or until a serious breakdown happens, right? Instead, you proactively check the vehicle and take care of it in a preventive manner to avoid future problems, improve performance and ensure that your drive is smooth and safe. Exactly the same with your website.

Such a test helps to understand if all the components of the site - inclusive loading speedDesigncontentSearch Engine Optimization (SEO) And more - work in the optimal way. If problems are discovered, they can be fixed before they become serious problems that can harm the visibility of the site, the user experience and the ability of the site to produce better results.

In addition, site testing can reveal opportunities for improvement that are tailored specifically to your needs. For example, improving the site's loading speed can lead to an improvement in search engine rankings, which can increase the number of visitors to the site. On the other hand, an improvement in the user interface and the navigation experience can lead to an improvement in the users' desire to stay on the site and make additional purchases or actions.

eventually, Website check It is an important tool for continuous improvement andRegular maintenance of the site, and provides you with the tools to avoid future problems, maximize the site's potential and keep it relevant and effective over time.

The huge importance of website inspection:

Your website, like any digital system, may suffer from various technical problems - broken links, pages that do not load, code errors, security problems and more. A comprehensive site inspection is the way to avoid such problems and anticipate a cure for the blow. Many times, such problems are detected even before the surfers or the search engines encounter them, and this can make a significant difference in improving the site's performance.

If your site is slow, unresponsive or difficult to navigate, you may lose surfers quickly, which may harm the user experience. Testing a site allows you to understand how to improve the browsing experience and make the site more pleasant and accessible, so that surfers stay longer and leave less.

Another critical point is SEO. Google ranks websites according to hundreds of parameters, and if there are technical problems or in the content of the website, it can damage its ranking in the search engines. A comprehensive SEO test helps to identify such problems and give you the tools to fix them, which will improve the site's position in the search results and increase exposure and reach to the site.

Nowadays, most surfers enter websites through mobile devices, so a website that is not optimized for mobile simply will not be able to provide a good browsing experience. A test verifies that your website is responsive - that is, that its design and function are suitable for all types of devices and screens.

Site loading speed It is not only a matter of convenience - it is also a factor that helps to improve the site's ranking in Google. Slow sites make surfers leave faster, which hurts conversion rates. A speed test, for example with tools like Google PageSpeed ​​Insights, can identify problems with the site's function and offer solutions for improvement.

In addition, it is important to check the Website security. A website that is not secure may be exposed to attacks, and this not only endangers the information of the surfers, but also damages the reputation of the website. Google prefers secure sites (those that use HTTPS), and this also has an impact on rankings.

regarding accessibility, a site that is not accessible to people with disabilities not only misses an important target audience, but may also violate the law. An inspection will verify that the site complies with the relevant standards, such as standard 5568 in Israel, and will allow you to reach more surfers legally.

In addition to correcting existing problems, a comprehensive inspection may also reveal new opportunities. Maybe there is content that could be improved or new keywords that could improve the site's ranking. It can also help you understand how users behave on the site and what improvements should be made to maximize the site's success.

The digital world is constantly changing, and the competitors do not stop for a moment. Periodic tests Helping you stay up to date and adapt the site to changes in the algorithms of the search engines, so that you maintain a competitive advantage over time.

After all, neglecting site testing is like neglecting it Maintenance of an expensive vehicle. This can lead to problems that will harm the ratings, cause a loss of surfers and harm the reputation of the site - and finally also to financial losses.

What does a comprehensive site inspection include? The ultimate checklist

  • Technical SEO testing: This test focuses on the technical basis of the website, and makes sure that the search engines can crawl and index it. Make sure there are no technical barriers that prevent the important pages from being scanned. Includes checking the robots.txt file, sitemap.xml file, 404 errors, and Google index metrics.
  • SEO check inside the page: This is an analysis of the elements within each page, to improve relevance to keywords and increase the user experience. Among the topics examined: use of keywords in titles, meta descriptions, image optimization, URL structure, and ensuring quality and focused content.
  • Offsite SEO testing: This test focuses on incoming links to the site, and includes an analysis of their quality and nature, as well as the identity of the sources from which the links come. In addition, the presence of the brand in social networks and mentions of the brand throughout the Internet are examined.
  • Content check: This stage includes an in-depth analysis of the content on the site, with a focus on performance analysis and organic browsing. In order to find gaps in the content, outdated content, or content that requires improvement. In addition, it must be verified that the content meets the users' intent at different stages in the customer journey.
  • User Experience (UX) Testing: This review focuses on the various aspects of the surfer's experience, including site navigation, content readability, accessibility for people with disabilities, the mobile experience, and site speed. The purpose of the review is to make sure that the surfer can get the most out of the site in an intuitive and convenient way.

Google PageSpeed ​​Insights (PSI): A must-have tool in the tester's arsenal

As we have seen, site speed and performance are an integral part of comprehensive testing. Google PageSpeed ​​Insights is a free and popular tool from Google, designed for exactly this purpose. Its importance stems from several reasons:

An official Google tool: It reflects what Google considers important in terms of performance and technical user experience. Its metrics (Core Web Vitals) are official ranking factors.

Laboratory data and field data: PSI provides two types of data:

  1. Laboratory data: are based on a controlled test that simulates loading a page under certain conditions (using a tool called Lighthouse). Useful for detecting real-time performance issues. The overall score (0-100) is mainly based on laboratory data.
  2. area data: Based on anonymous data collected from real Chrome users who visited the site in the last 28 days. This data reflects the real user experience and is what Google uses mainly for ranking. This data is only available for sites with sufficient traffic.

Clear grades and recommendations: The tool gives a numerical score (0-100) for mobile and desktop performance, and clearly indicates (green, orange, red) whether the indicators meet Google's goals. In addition, it provides a list of "opportunities" and "diagnoses" - concrete recommendations for technical improvements.

Focus on Core Web Vitals: The tool places special emphasis on the core indicators (LCP, INP/FID, CLS) that are important for ranking.

Easy to use: Just enter a URL and get a detailed report in minutes.

How to interpret the PSI report?

: It is important to check the results in both tabs. For the most part, mobile scores are lower and more important to Google ("Mobile-First Indexing").

: Area data (if available) can be seen for the specific URL being checked or for the entire site (Origin).

The overall score (0-100): gives a general indication. A score above 90 is considered good, 50-89 requires improvement, and below 50 is considered bad. However, it's important not to obsess about the 100 score. The goal is to improve the real user experience, not just the synthetic score.

: Check if the site "passes" the evaluation of the core indicators based on the area data. This is the most important goal.

: This is the heart of the report. Go through the recommendations, understand what they say and try to implement the ones that have the biggest impact (the tool indicates the potential savings in loading time).

Using PSI as part of the inspection process: The PSI test is an essential step within the test of theTechnical SEO. The findings of the report should be translated into concrete tasks for the development team or the website promoter, such as: optimizing images, implementing lazy loading, improving CSS/JS code, Upgrading the storage server, advanced caching settings and more.

The process of performing a site inspection: step by step

Performing a comprehensive test requires a systematic approach:

1. Defining goals and scope

Before diving into the data, it is important to define what you want to achieve from the test:

  • Targeting specific areas: Is the goal to improve speed, increase organic traffic or conversion rate optimization (CRO)?
  • Coordination of expectations: Defining the indicators (KPIs) for success at the end of the process.

2. Equipping yourself with essential tools

To get a complete picture, a combination of several tools must be used:

  • Management and measurement: (for scan and index data) and (for user behavior analysis).
  • Technical scanning (Crawlers): tools like or To identify code and structure errors.
  • SEO analysis includes: Platforms like or For keyword research and link analysis.
  • Performance and speed: or

3. Data collection and analysis

  • Collection: Running the tools and centralizing the information by categories: technical, on-page, off-page, content and UX.
  • Analysis: Identifying patterns, anomalies and opportunities. At this stage it is important to understand the **"why"** behind the numbers and not just the "what".

4. Creating a report and action plan

Organizing the findings into an orderly working document that includes:

  • Executive summary: Summary of the current situation.
  • Prioritization: The ranking of the problems according to severity level and potential impact against the implementation effort.
  • Roadmap: A list of concrete tasks, schedules and definition of responsible persons.

5. Implementation, monitoring and control

  • Execution: Implementing the changes on the website according to the established priority.
  • Continuous monitoring: Checking a site is not a one-time operation. Performance should continue to be monitored to ensure that improvements have produced results and to identify new challenges in real time.

The devastating consequences of neglecting website testing

What happens if you decide to "save" time and resources and not perform periodic site inspections? The results can be painful:

  1. Drop in Google rankings: Unaddressed technical issues, outdated content, or poor user experience may cause Google to downgrade a site. Professional SEO services can prevent it.
  2. Negative user experience: Surfers may encounter errors, long loading times or navigational difficulties, which will cause them to give up and leave the competitors' site.
  3. Damage to conversion rates: A slow and inefficient website will make it difficult for surfers to complete desired actions (such as purchasing or leaving details), which will lead to a loss of revenue. Sponsored advertising on Google It won't help if the landing page is slow.
  4. Aggravating technical problems: A small problem that is not dealt with today could turn into a big crisis tomorrow and sometimes even disable the website.
  5. security risks: Neglecting updates and security checks may expose the site to hacking, information theft and damage to reputation. Managed storage with ongoing maintenance protects against these risks.
  6. lagging behind competitors: While you are neglecting the site, your competitors are investing in improvement and progressing at your expense.

AEO and SEO: Adapting to the smart search era

This article was written with SEO (Search Engine Optimization) and AEO (Answer Engine Optimization / AI Engine Optimization) in mind. While SEO focuses on optimizing for traditional search engines, AEO refers to optimizing for answer engines and AI-based virtual assistants, as well as adapting to how AI understands and ranks content.

A comprehensive site inspection supports both aspects:

  • Strong technical base (SEO/AEO): AI engines also need an accessible, fast, secure and well-structured website to crawl and understand the content.
  • Quality content and meets user intent (SEO/AEO): Focusing on creating in-depth, reliable, well-structured content (with titles, lists) that directly answers user questions is essential for both areas.
  • Structured data (SEO/AEO): Schema Markup helps both traditional and AI search engines understand the context of information more accurately.
  • User experience (SEO/AEO): Even if AI finds the answer on your site, if the user experience on the site is bad, the surfer (and the AI) may prefer another source. Speed ​​(Core Web Vitals) is a key part of this.

A properly performed site test ensures that your site is not only adapted to today's algorithms, but also to the future of search based more and more on semantic understanding and artificial intelligence.

Summary: Website testing is an investment, not an expense

A comprehensive website audit is not a luxury, but a strategic necessity. This is a thorough process that examines the health of the site, its efficiency and the user experience it offers. The purpose of the test is to locate and correct problems, improve performance and take advantage of opportunities, while examining every aspect of the site - from technical aspects such as scanning and indexing, to optimizing content and tags and analyzing incoming links.

Tools like Google PageSpeed ​​Insights are part of the process, and provide critical insights into speed and performance - direct factors that affect user satisfaction and the site's ranking in search engines.

Neglecting periodic tests can lead to digital decline, but investing in a comprehensive test and implementing its recommendations is a direct investment in the success of the business. Such a test will lead to a fast, user-friendly site, with higher visibility in search engines, and ultimately - a site that converts better and achieves its business goals.

Don't wait for your website to "break down". Be proactive, do a comprehensive inspection today andUpgrade your digital asset So that it operates at its full potential and serves you in the competitive age of the Internet.

title: SEO 2026: How to Appear in Google AI Overviews
content:
The end of the era of "links" and the beginning of the era of "answers"

Do you remember the days when all you had to do was write a short article, push a few keywords and get a sea of ​​surfers? Welcome to 2026. Today, Google is no longer just a "bulletin board" that points to websites - it has become an engine that provides answers (SGE). Instead of scrolling and going from website to website, surfers receive a smart summary from the artificial intelligence (AI) already at the top of the page, which saves them time and the need to click.

for us approxDigital marketing agency, the challenge has changed: the goal is no longer just 'to be first on Google' (Important to understand: a site can be ranked first in the regular organic search results, and still be left out of the AI ​​review that appears above it), but to become the most authoritative source that the AI ​​chooses to draw its answers from.

In this article we will try to explain the The dramatic changes that happen below the surface of Google, and we will reveal the strategy we implement to ensure that our customers are 'the answer' - even in a world where everyone is used to getting solutions without clicking.

It is important to remember: The rules of the game have changed. The world of traditional SEO has evolved into the era of AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) and GEO (Artificial Intelligence Engine Optimization). If once the goal was only to "appear in the results", today the goal is to become the most qualified source displayed within the SGE - that intelligent Google AI answer box that provides the surfer with an immediate solution.

This is a whole network of integrated operations that is difficult to contain in one article, but here we will explain the principles that every business owner must know to be present in this new arena.

A word of transparencyThis article was created to provide you with knowledge and tools to help you make the best decisions for your business. Transparency is a top value for us. Therefore, it is important for us to point out that while the text is compiled with the help of advanced artificial intelligence technologies, it has been carefully checked and human edited by Adwrks 365's team of experts. The goal is to ensure that the information you receive is as accurate, relevant and useful as possible. Fun and educational reading!

The revolution of AEO (Answer Engine Optimization)

In 2026, we are no longer just optimizing for search engines, but moving toEngine optimizationanswers. Google's AI is no longer content with displaying a list of links; He is looking for "Information Nuggets", which are actually answers that are both accurate, both reliable and presented in a way that is easy to digest in an instant.

How do you turn the information on the website into the first answers that the surfer will see?

  • Structure of a "question and answer": Today's surfers ask specific questions - "Which work shoe is the safest?" or "How do you invest in real estate in 2026?". For your information to be selected, each paragraph must directly address the searcher's need. The more focused you are, the more the AI ​​will trust you as a source of authority.
  • Schemas (Schema Markup) - the digital identity card: In 2026, the hidden code on the site is our way of proving to Google that the information comes from a real person with proven experience. If we do not specify to Google who is behind the words (Person Schema) and what is his expertise, the information may be lost in a sea of ​​generic content.
  • Accuracy and reliability in a fraction of a second: The AI ​​prefers to provide users with information that has been proven to be reliable. This means a combination of real data, customer recommendations and a direct connection to reality on the ground. When the information is presented correctly, the surfer gets exactly what he was looking for, and your business becomes his first address.
  • The new arena: it's not just Google anymore: It is important to understand - the search in 2026 does not begin and end with the familiar Google search box. Your customers today ask questions directly to language models (LLMs) such as Gemini, ChatGPT, Claude or Perplexity. They ask for recommendations such as: "Who is the recommended digital agency in Karmiel?" or "Which work shoe is recommended for prolonged standing in field conditions?".

This is where the concept of LLM Optimization comes into play. The big language models don't "crawl" your site in real time like an old search engine, but they rely on a knowledge base and cross data from all over the web. If your business is not defined as a strong "entity" in forums, reviews and professional articles - these models simply will not recognize your existence and will not be able to recommend you. GEO optimization ensures that your information is accessible, verified and preferred by all existing AI models.

Building a business entity (Entity Building) - the key to authority in the age of AI

The revolution of 2026: Google no longer ranks websites - it ranks entities

To understand how Google works today, you have to stop thinking about "website" and start thinking about "entity". An entity is a brand that has cross evidence of its existence in both the digital and physical worlds. Google looks for the DNA of the brand within the content to decide: "Is this a brand I can trust?".

What does it actually look like? Study Case of "Amiam" company:

When we started, for months we built a strong SEO infrastructure for "Amiam": we improved the website's visibility, created professional content and built a high-quality link network. This work paid off - the site began to appear in Google's AI results as a leading authority in the field of work clothes and a shop for work clothes, work shoes and professional safety equipment.

But how do you "lock" this status as an authority in a certain field? This is where a step comes in entity validation. We didn't settle for just good content, but we performed full synchronization of all brand data:

  • Physical data cross: We have connected the official digital ID of The business on Google Maps directly into the site code and articles.
  • Location and identity verification: We have synchronized the physical address and official details of the business with every mention of the brand across the network.
  • Trust Signals: We linked the real customer recommendations with the professional content on the site.

The result: The combination between months of SEO work and the technical "soldering" to the physical entity created a complete picture for Google. Now, when the AI ​​pulls information from the site, it knows for sure that the answer comes from experts with proven knowledge and reputation, and not a sparse generic content site created by bots or not professionally enough.

Bottom line: if your site already appears in AI, that's great, but it doesn't guarantee you stability.

To keep your place, you must connect all the endpoints: from the content and links to your physical identity on the maps. Only a verified entity survives the algorithm updates that are made from time to time by Google.

And more than that - those who do not advance, may be hurt. The promotion methods of the previous decade, such as keyword compression or massive link building without context, have not only stopped working - they are becoming a "red flag" for Google. In today's system, Google may penalize or marginalize sites that are perceived as "thin content" or as those that try to "cheat" the algorithm. If your site has not been optimized for the SGE and GEO era, you not only risk a drop in ranking, but a complete disappearance from the AI ​​reviews.

Quality over quantity: Why is 1,500 words worth more than 50 AI articles in 2026?

Like many who ask, you are probably thinking right now: "How can you produce more professional content than a bot that has access to all the databases?". The answer is simple: the AI ​​is a machine for recycling information, it does not "live" the area. The Google of 2026 is no longer looking for summaries of what everyone else has already written, it is searching Added value that only a human can give.

Google has developed an "Effort Detection" algorithm that knows how to differentiate between generic text and content that has been thought about. For the AI ​​to choose to quote you, the article must include what the bot will never have:

  • Real world experience: Bot knows how to cite safety standards, but he is unable to describe how a certain model of shoe behaves in a realistic test in extreme field conditions. Google gives priority to those who bring with them first-hand insights - knowledge gained from doing and practical experience, and not just from dry data collection.
  • Original data and graphs: Instead of using data that everyone knows, we combine graphs, aggregated data and screenshots from real work processes ("what happens in the field"). An original picture of the business in action is worth more to the algorithm than 1,000 words of a bot.
  • The personal angle and expertise: The AI ​​cannot say "I think the market is wrong". You do. Google is looking for expert opinion and the ability to take a complex subject and make it accessible in a simple and innovative way.

The bottom line: The AI ​​sounds like an encyclopedia; We make sure your content sounds like Expert consultant. This is the difference between an article that is swallowed on the net and one that becomes an answer that Google will present to surfers.

Not just technology: how do you preserve an entity's authority over time?

Building an entity is not a single or one-time operation, but a whole network of integrated operations that require constant synchronization. In 2026, Google examines your business every moment anew, it cross-checks data to make sure you are still active, reliable and relevant.

In order for your brand to continue to lead and appear in the AI ​​reviews, you need to carry out ongoing entity maintenance, which ensures that all "network edges" from the website to the business profiles transmit uniform and consistent authority.

  • Consistency is the name of the game (NAP): Google acts like a detective cross-checking data. Make sure that the business name, address and phone number appear exactly the same everywhere on the web: from the official website to the smallest indexes. Any discrepancy in the information is a "red light" that may cause the AI ​​to stop recommending the business.
  • Reviews as fuel for AI: The reviews on Google Business have long been more than just "stars". Google's AI analyzes the content of the reviews; If a customer writes "the most comfortable work shoes I've ever bought", Google connects this recommendation directly to the relevant product on the site. Proper management of surfers' feedback makes them a digital authority for the brand.
  • To be the "encyclopedia" of your field: In order for Google to mark a business as an "expert in its field", it must cover all the questions and needs of the surfers. The more professional content that meets different angles of the field is created, the more the AI ​​understands that this is the most qualified source and its preferred answer.

The bottom line: Building an entity is the key to entering the world of AI, but maintaining it together is what ensures you stay on top. In an age where technology changes every week, your verified entity is the most stable digital asset you have.

Not Just Typing: The Voice and Visual Search Revolution

How do you adapt the site to the world of sound and images?

"Ok Google, find me Recommended digital marketing agency in Karmiel". In 2026, this is what an average search will look like. We no longer just type single words into the search box, but conduct a dialogue with our devices. For the site to appear in these results, it must "speak" in a language that the AI ​​understands.

  • To speak "human language": Instead of focusing on dry keywords, you should build content that answers natural questions. The more the content on the website is built in the structure of a human conversation (like "question and answer" paragraphs), the easier it is for the artificial intelligence to pull you out as the "winning answer" in a voice search.
  • Google "sees" and decodes the visual: In 2026, Google is no longer just "guessing" what is in the image - it is analyzing it in depth. In order to maximize exposure, every image on the website should be double optimized:
  1. Visual scan: The AI ​​analyzes the objects within the image (for example, recognizes that it is a crane or a brokerage office).
  2. Professional ALT text: Providing an accurate behind-the-scenes textual explanation that describes the context of the image to the AI. This combination ensures that if a surfer uses (search by photo), your brand will rise in the results thanks to accurate visual identification.
  • Local and digital authority: In voice search, Google prioritizes businesses that it recognizes as a real, certified "entity" with a defined physical location. Connecting the digital identity to the professional content on the website creates for Google a "trusted address" - one that can be confidently recommended to the end user.

User Experience (Core Web Vitals 2.0)

Speed ​​and surfing experience: in 2026 there is no place for slow people

After the last upgrade, Google tightened the requirements: the speed of the site is no longer only for the surfers, but is a threshold condition for Google itself. While the official standard (LCP) defines a charge of up to 2.5 seconds As a normal score, in the age of AI the aspiration is to drop well below that. Google's bots scan the web at crazy speed, and if your site loads slowly, they will simply "skip" it and move to the next site to save time and computing resources.

This is not only for the organic promotion and user experience - it directly affects Google Ads as well! It is important to understand that all Google systems talk to each other. We recently encountered a case of a client whose sponsored ads were repeatedly disqualified for the reason "Target is inactive". The problem was not that the site fell, but that its loading rate was so slow that the Google bot could not complete the scan and performed a "time-out". For Google, a page that loads too slowly is an invalid page. Only after technical optimization and speed improvement was carried out, Google was able to crawl the site and the campaigns started running again.

In the end, speed is not just a code, it is an estimate of your surfer's time, one of the most valuable resources today. We at the agency see this over and over again: websites that are well built and load quickly, convey the right message in the first fraction of a second and transmit reliability and professionalism even before the surfer has read a single word. The AI ​​does know how to measure seconds, but only humans know how to appreciate a smooth experience that truly respects them.

A fast website that loads in a fraction of a second is your main key to getting on the AI ​​answer list and ensuring that all advertising systems work optimally for you.

A little tip from experts: To help Google immediately understand who you are and where you are, you should add your map and the exact business details at the bottom of the site (the firer). This helps the artificial intelligence to easily connect your website with the business in reality, which significantly increases your credibility in the eyes of Google.

The future is here: is your business presence ready for 2026?

Google's transition from ranking "sites" to ranking of business and authority is the new rules of the game. Sites that continue to operate in the old ways, without connecting their content to a verified identity and proven experience in the field, will simply be pushed out of the AI ​​and voice search results.

We already see this happening in the field with some of our customers, such as AmiyamHasdai lifting cranesNexus Business Real Estate or Express transports in Jerusalem, already appear as the preferred choice in Google's AI summaries. It is the combination between in-depth expert content and the establishment of their digital identity that turned them from "another search result" into an authority in their field - one that artificial intelligence chooses to present at the forefront of its answers.

So what is the next step for you? Don't wait for the next Google update. Start building your presence today:

  • Verify the identity of the business: Make sure that Google understands exactly who you are and what your expertise is on every page of the site.
  • Connect the physical address to the digital one: Make sure your position and professional authority is attached to every piece of content.
  • Demonstrate authority (E-E-A-T): Make sure that your practical experience is visible - both to surfers and to Google bots.

Investing in your business presence is not only "Website promotion", is your brand's insurance certificate in a world dominated by artificial intelligence.

title: Website Speed & PageSpeed Score Improvements in 2026
content:
In the digital world of 2026, speed is no longer a "bonus" - it is a condition of survival. If in the past we were talking about seconds, today we are talking about milliseconds. Google, through its advanced AI models, is no longer just scanning keywords; It "experiences" your website in real time. A slow site is a site that Google will simply stop displaying, therefore Improving site speed It has become the most critical element in your digital strategy - without it, the website simply hurts the user experience that Google is trying to provide and is pushed back.

It is important to understand: speed is not only a matter of organic promotion (SEO). Recently we are encountering more and more cases of them Google Ads Automatically disqualifies ads due to long load times. We have encountered clients whose campaign simply stopped because Google marked the link as "Destination Not Working". From the point of view of the system, if the site does not load within a few seconds, it is simply considered a broken site. The meaning? The business loses exposure, inquiries and money - just because of a slow infrastructure.

In this guide, we're on a team We will dive into the technical and strategic depth of performance optimization. It's not just about installing one or another plugin, but a deep understanding of how browsers, sponsored campaigns and AI scanners work today.

A word of transparencyThis article was created to provide you with knowledge and tools to help you make the best decisions for your business. Transparency is a top value for us. Therefore, it is important for us to point out that while the text is compiled with the help of advanced artificial intelligence technologies, it has been carefully checked and human edited by Adwrks 365's team of experts. The goal is to ensure that the information you receive is as accurate, relevant and useful as possible. Fun and educational reading!

Why is site speed critical to SEO and AI crawlability?

Google has moved to full use of (Search Generative Experience). This means that artificial intelligence doesn't just "scan" your website, it analyzes it in real time to provide direct answers to users. If your site is heavy or loaded with unnecessary code, the AI ​​bots "get tired". In the professional language it is called (Crawling budget) – Google has a limited amount of resources to devote to crawling. so, Improving site speed It is no longer just a matter of convenience, but a technical necessity: if the site is slow, the bot will scan only a small part of the pages, and your important information will simply not reach the AI's answer engine.

The Core Web Vitals in 2026: The metrics that determine your ranking

In 2026, Google is no longer looking only at "when the site was up", but at how it feels. When approaching the process of Improving site speed, these are the three indicators that must be in the center (and are especially critical for WordPress and Elementor sites):

  • The index that checks when the main content (like the hero image or the title) is shown to the surfer. In 2026, the target is under 1.2 seconds. Any deviation from this signals to Google that your site is "not ready for work".
  • This is the index that finally replaced the old FID. It checks the site's dynamism: when a surfer presses a button or opens a menu, how long does the site take to respond? A "frozen" site where the surfer clicks and waits, will suffer a dramatic drop in ratings.
  • You know when you press a button and suddenly the whole page "pops up" because an advertisement or image has been loaded? This is the CLS. Google is very strict with sites that pop up, because it is seen as a poor user experience and even misleading.

The technical infrastructure: why is your storage the real bottleneck?

Optimizing a website can be compared to improving a racing car: you can change to expensive tires and improve the aerodynamics (plugins and code), but if the engine (server) is weak and old - you will never win the race. In 2026, Google measures the – The time it takes for your server to even start responding. If your server responds slowly, all other optimizations you make will be meaningless.

Our technology choice: VPS server from uPress

As someone who manages dozens of websites, we do not compromise on storage quality. on-, we use the infrastructure of , and specifically on my server (virtual private server) customized to our needs.

Unlike regular shared hosting where you "share" resources with hundreds of other sites (causing sudden slowdowns), the uPress VPS server gives us processing power and memory dedicated solely to our site. This allows us to serve the site at maximum speed even under a load of surfers or intensive bot scans.

What makes storage "2026 ready"?

  • Moving to NVMe technology: If your hosting company is still using regular SSD drives, your site is living in the past. NVMe drives are several times faster and allow the WordPress database to retrieve information in a fraction of a second.
  • HTTP/3 protocol (QUIC): This is the new generation of network data transfer. It allows the browser to download all website components (images, code, text) simultaneously and securely. This is standard on the servers we manage.
  • Latest PHP version: WordPress ran on the PHP language. Each version update (such as the move to 8.2 and above) brings tens of percent speed improvements in the server's memory management.

The DNS: the fastest path to your website

A common mistake is to use the domain registrar's default DNS servers. on-, we combine the power of uPress servers together with . why? Because the DNS is the "phone book" of the Internet. The faster the browser finds your server address, the sooner the loading will start. This is a "free" improvement that can save hundreds of critical milliseconds before the first code is even loaded.

Expert tip: Cheap storage at $5 a month is often the most expensive expense of your business. It costs you in Google placements, sponsored ad rejections and customers who leave the site out of frustration. Investing in a quality server is the investment with the highest ROI you can make for the website.

Optimization of assets: how to handle images and video without damaging the design?

In ranking the slowness factors of WordPress sites, the weight of the media is almost always in first place. Over 70% of average page weight comes from unoptimized images. In 2026, uploading a JPEG image directly from your camera or stock is simply a "crime" against your SEO. Google and its AI crawlers are looking for lightweight websites, and heavy images are the fastest way to get a red PageSpeed ​​score.

Beyond the next generation formats: WebP and AVIF

The new standard requires a complete transition to modern formats that allow high quality and zero weight:

  • A format that reduces the weight of the image by about 30% compared to JPEG, without the human eye noticing the difference.
  • The most advanced format today. This is a standard that manages to achieve even better compression performance than WebP. It is important to make sure Every image uploaded to the site is converted to these formats as part of the upload process.

Lazy Loading technology - but smart

A common mistake is to apply Lazy Loading comprehensively to all images on the site. Why is this a mistake? Because if you put "lazy loading" on the main image (the Hero Image), you will directly hurt the LCP index. How do you do it right? Define an exception for images that appear "above the fold" (Above the Fold) so that they are loaded immediately, while all other visual assets are loaded only when the surfer starts scrolling. This saves valuable loading time and bandwidth resources.

And what about video?

Video is a potential "performance killer" if not managed correctly:

  1. Avoid uploading video directly to the server: Even with a powerful VPS server (like the one we run at uPress), video loaded directly from storage creates unnecessary load.
  2. Using Smart Embed (Facade): Instead of loading the entire heavy YouTube or Vimeo player immediately upon opening the page, a static image is used that replaces the player. Only as soon as the surfer presses the play button, the heavy scripts are loaded. This technique alone can boost the PageSpeed ​​score by tens of points.

Defining dimensions (Explicit Width & Height)

to improve the index of (page stability), the browser must know in advance the size of the image that is about to be loaded. Without setting exact dimensions in the HTML, the page will "jump" as soon as the image appears and the text moves. Making sure to set the height and width for each visual element ensures a smooth and stable loading.

The expert angle: Optimizing images isn't just about "shrinking". It's a matter of submitting the right image, in the right size (Responsive Images), to the right device. A mobile surfer does not need to download a 4K resolution image that fits a huge computer screen - this is a waste of resources that Google punishes him for.

Cleaning "background noise": optimization of JS and CSS files (the heart of the problem in Elementor)

If the storage is the engine and the images are the chassis, then the code (JS and CSS) is the "cargo" that the site carries. The main problem with WordPress sites based on page builders like Elementor is "code bloat" (). The site loads hundreds of lines of code designed to activate widgets or designs that do not exist at all on the specific page the surfer is viewing.

How do you clean up the code without "breaking" the site?

Proper optimization requires real surgery in the website code:

  • Conditional loading of assets: This is one of the most effective steps. The idea is to eliminate loading of unnecessary CSS and JS files on pages that are not needed. For example: if you don't have a contact form on the home page, there is no reason for the Contact Form 7 or Elementor Forms code to be loaded there. Each file that is deleted saves valuable time for Google's AI scanners and makes it easier on the mobile device's processor.
  • Handling Render-Blocking Resources: These are the resources that "block" the rise of the site. The browser stops everything to read them before displaying content to the browser. The professional solution is to transfer non-critical files to the end of loading () or charging them at the same time (). This way the surfer sees the content immediately, and the design "decorations" are loaded a fraction of a second later.
  • Minification: The process of removing spaces, comments, and unnecessary characters from code. Although it sounds negligible, the accumulation of thousands of lines of code becomes a significant mass that affects the processing speed.
  • Disabling native Google Fonts and Emoji: WordPress loads files by default that are not always required. It is recommended to store the fonts locally on a fast server (as we do in our VPS infrastructure at uPress), which saves unnecessary requests to external servers and speeds up the LCP index considerably.

Elementor's challenge in 2026

Although Elementor has made a leap forward with the Containers mechanism, it still tends to load heavy libraries. To achieve peak performance, you must take advantage of the (experimental settings) of Elementor intelligently and enable features like and- - Only after a full compatibility check.

Expert tip: Do not install a "speed add-on" and activate all its options at once. This is the sure recipe for breaking the website's design. Real optimization is done in layers, while constantly checking that the site functions perfectly both on mobile and on the computer after each change.

The Strategy Behind the Score: Why PageSpeed ​​Isn't Everything?

A common mistake of website owners is a blind pursuit of the "green number" (score 100) in Google's measurement tool. While a high score is a good indication, the real goal is The actual user experience. A site can receive a score of 95 but feel "stuck" to the surfer, and vice versa - a site with a score of 85 can feel lightning fast.

The difference between technical speed and perceived speed (Perceived Performance)

In the SEO world of 2026, we emphasize that the surfer receives an initial interaction as quickly as possible.

  • Gradual loading: The goal is to display "Above the Fold" in less than a second. As soon as the surfer starts reading the title or seeing the main image, the Google bots and the AI ​​already understand that the website provides value.
  • Prevention of "stasis" (TBT): We check the Total Blocking Time. This is the time when the browser is busy processing code and does not allow the surfer to click on anything. Reducing this index is what differentiates a frustrating site from a fun site to browse.

What does a professional optimization process look like?

Instead of magic solutions, thorough work looks like this:

  1. Deep diagnosis: Not just running a test in PageSpeed ​​Insights, but analyzing Waterfall reports to understand exactly which file is delaying loading.
  2. Infrastructure care: Alignment at the server level (as we mentioned in the storage section).
  3. Optimization of the page structure (DOM): Reducing the number of elements on the page. A site with thousands of HTML elements will always be slower, no matter how many memory plugins are installed on it.
  4. Tests on weak devices: A website that looks fast on your new iPhone 16 may crawl on a 3-year-old Android device. True optimization is measured on the weakest device.

A point to think about: When you see a site with a score of 90 or higher, it's no accident. This is the result of proper planning where the design does not come at the expense of performance, but works together with them.

Personal example: speed as a standard of excellence

At our agency, we don't just talk about performance - we implement it. To meet Google's strictest standards for 2026, we have implemented a process Improving site speed Aggressive to our agency site, with the goal of reaching the limit of technological ability.

The results speak for themselves

PageSpeed ​​Insights score on a computer (Desktop):

  • Final score:perfect!
  • Visual load time (LCP): only 0.5 seconds (almost instantly!).
  • Page Blocking Time (TBT): standing on

PageSpeed ​​Insights Score on Mobile:

  • Final score:
  • Visual load time (LCP): standing on 2.1 seconds (in the green and strict range).
  • Page Blocking Time (TBT): standing on

How did we do it? We have integrated advanced server infrastructures, a full transition to the WebP image format, and smart management of JavaScript resources (Delayed Loading). The result is a site that loads almost instantly, provides a smooth user experience and is ranked at the technological top of Google.

Summary: The road to a fast website in 2026 starts today

improvement Site speed It is not a "Zabang and we're done" project. It is a continuous process of maintenance, control and adaptation to the changing technologies of Google and the world of AI. As we have seen, speed affects every aspect of your digital business: from the positions in the organic search results, through the approval of the ads In Google Ads And to the profit line and the conversion of surfers to paying customers.

The combination between a strong storage infrastructure (such as a dedicated VPS server), technical optimization of code and media, and an understanding of the new user experience metrics, is the winning formula for a site that not only survives in 2026, but leads the market.

Summary checklist - what can be done now?

  • Performance test: Run your site in PageSpeed ​​Insights and look at the Mobile data (the really important ones).
  • The storage exam: Check if your server supports HTTP/3 and current PHP versions.
  • Weight reduction: Make sure that all the images on the site are in WebP format and that there are no heavy videos that are loaded directly from the server.
  • Professional advice: Sometimes, the problem lies deep within the code or the site template, and in these cases a professional hand is required who knows how to perform the "analysis" without harming the site's activity.

title: Paid Search vs Organic SEO — A Comparison
content:
For most business owners, the world of digital marketing feels like a collection of complicated concepts: SEO, PPC, "organic is dead" or "sponsored is expensive." These terms mainly create confusion, when at the end of the bottom line you are only interested in one question: Where to invest the budget to get more customers at minimum cost? This question is complex, but the experience we have gained in managing hundreds of projects allows us to put the data in order for you.

In this article we will review the two main marketing methods: organic promotion (SEO) and paid promotion (PPC). We will explain the costs of each of them, we will detail the factors that affect the price (such as the level of competition in the field and the authority of the site), and we will present the differences between them in a simple way. At the end of the page you will find smart calculator that will help you get a personalized budget estimate for your data, so that you can make a decision that is based on numbers and not on feelings.

A word of transparencyThis article was created to provide you with knowledge and tools to help you make the best decisions for your business. Transparency is a top value for us. Therefore, it is important for us to point out that while the text is compiled with the help of advanced artificial intelligence technologies, it has been carefully checked and human edited by Adwrks 365's team of experts. The goal is to ensure that the information you receive is as accurate, relevant and useful as possible. Fun and educational reading!

What is SEO anyway?

the initials (Search Engine Optimization) means in Hebrew: "Optimization for search engines". In simple language, this is the way to make your website appear in Google's search results naturally (organically), without paying money for every time someone clicks on your website.

When we search for something on Google, we usually look at the first three results. The goal of the organic promotion is to convince Google that your site is the most accurate and high-quality answer to what the surfer was looking for, so that it places you at the top of the list.

This is a long-term process. Imagine that you are building a reputation as an expert in your field: it doesn't happen in a day, but once the market (and Google) recognizes you as an authority, customers start coming to you on their own. Unlike sponsored advertising that disappears as soon as you stop paying, organic promotion builds you a digital asset that continues to work for you 24/7.

The crucial elements for successful organic promotion:

  • Valuable content: Writing professional and up-to-date information that provides a real solution to your surfers' searches.
  • Technical optimization: Code settings, loading speed and correct website structure that allow Google's crawlers to understand the website easily.
  • User Experience (UX): A website that is designed correctly, optimized for mobile and very easy to navigate.
  • Authority and links (Backlinks): Creating "recommendations" from other websites that link to you and confirm to Google that you are the most reliable source in the field.

What is paid promotion (PPC)?

Sponsored Promotion, also known as (Pay Per Click), is a method in which you pay platforms such as Google or Facebook to appear at the top of the search results or in the surfers' feed immediately.

If the organic promotion is a process of building reputation over time, the sponsored promotion is the "shortcut". Instead of waiting for Google to rank you naturally, you "rent" the first place. As we mentioned before - here you don't plant a tree and wait for it to grow, but simply buy the fruits on the spot.

The main features of the sponsored promotion:

  • Immediate results: From the moment the campaign went live, your ads appear and the phone can start ringing.
  • Pay per click model: You only pay when a surfer actually clicks on your ad and enters the site. If he only saw it and didn't click - you didn't pay.
  • Full control of the budget: You decide how much to spend each day. You can stop, activate or change the budget at any given moment.
  • Surgical precision (Targeting): It is possible to decide that the ads will appear only to a specific audience - for example, only to people aged 30-50 who live in Haifa and are looking for a certain service at this moment.

The great battle: organic promotion versus sponsored promotion - comparison table

To help you understand which method suits your goals right now, we have summarized the main differences in one simple table:

parameterorganic promotion (SEO)sponsored promotion (PPC)
Time for resultsGradual process (months)Immediate results (minutes)
short term costInvestment in building infrastructureDirect payment per click
long term costdecreasing (property already exists)remains constant (stop paying - disappear)
Position on the pagein the natural resultsat the top of the page (above all)
The trust of the surfershigh (perceived as an authority in the field)Medium (perceived as advertising content)
control of the messageDynamic (according to Google's considerations)complete (you determine each word)
measurabilitytrends and movement over timeMaximum accuracy (cost versus benefit)



When to choose sponsored promotion?

The sponsored promotion provides an answer to the need for immediate results. For new businesses or websites without a digital presence, this is the only way to appear at the top of the search results in a short period of time.

The main advantages of the method:

  1. Immediate availability Unlike the organic process which takes time, a sponsored campaign starts working as soon as it is approved. This is an essential tool for seasonal businesses (such as air conditioning technicians at the height of summer), for limited-time promotions or for the launch of a new service that needs exposure now.
  2. Target audience segmentation (Targeting) The system allows displaying the ad only to people who meet specific definitions: age, gender, geographic area and interests. This level of accuracy ensures that your budget will be directed to surfers with high conversion potential.
  3. Full control of expenses You determine the daily and monthly budget in advance. The system stops the advertising as soon as you have reached the ceiling you set, which allows you to manage the marketing cash flow in a complete way and increase or decrease the investment according to the amount of work in the business.

When to choose organic promotion?

The organic promotion is considered to build a digital asset that you own. If sponsored promotion is "renting" a place on Google, organic promotion is similar to owning profitable real estate in the city center - the more you invest in it, the more its value increases and your dependence on external payment decreases.

The main advantages of the method:

  1. Long-term economic efficiency (ROI). Unlike sponsored, where traffic stops as soon as the budget runs out, organic results continue to work for you over time. Once the site has established itself in high rankings, the cost of customer acquisition (CPA) drops significantly, as the clicks themselves are free of charge.
  2. Building authority and trust of surfers Many surfers tend to trust Google's natural results more than sponsored ads. Appearing at the top of the organic results positions your business as a professional authority in its field, which improves the chance that a customer will choose you over the competition even before you have spoken to them.
  3. Click through rates (CTR) are high The statistics show that despite the presence of the ads at the top of the page, a considerable part of the surfers skips them and clicks on the organic results. This means that presence in the organic top allows you to reach a significant market share of surfers who do not tend to click on advertisements.

The winning combination: 360° strategy

on-, our experience shows that the best results come from a combination of both methods. Instead of choosing a side, we harness the advantages of each of them to create a complementary marketing mechanism:

  • Using data for strategy accuracy: Through the sponsored campaigns we quickly identify which keywords actually generate sales (and not just traffic). We integrate this information into the organic promotion, to ensure that the long-term investment is focused on the most profitable phrases.
  • Taking over "real estate" in the search results: A double appearance - both in a sponsored ad and in an organic result - significantly increases the screen space of your business. Such a presence conveys power and authority, and increases the chance that the surfer will choose you.
  • Closing the circle with customers (Remarketing): The combination allows us to "return" potential customers. A surfer who came to the site through an organic result but did not make a purchase, will encounter a sponsored ad that will remind him of your business and motivate him to complete the action.

Summary: What is right for your business?

The choice between the two methods depends on your business goals:

  • Sponsored Promotion: Suitable for those who need immediate results, have a liquid advertising budget and are looking for full control over the rate of lead entry at any given moment.
  • organic promotion: A must for those who are building a long-term business, aspire to establish a leading brand in their field and want to significantly reduce the customer acquisition cost over time.

Our professional recommendation? The most effective way to grow is to start with sponsored promotion to "stir the wheels" and create an immediate flow of inquiries, while simultaneously investing in building the organic infrastructure. This combination ensures stable, consistent and healthy business growth.

Frequently asked questions and answers

What is the main difference between organic and sponsored promotion?
The main difference is in the payment model and the speed of the results. In sponsored promotion you pay for each click and the results are immediate, while in organic promotion you invest in building the site's long-term authority.
How long does it take to see results in organic promotion?
The organic promotion process usually takes between 4 and 9 months to see significant results. The time depends on the level of competition in the field, the seniority of the domain and the technical condition of the site.
What affects the price of website promotion?
The price is affected by the level of competition in the field, the amount of key phrases, the authority of the domain and the amount of content and links that need to be produced every month.
What is the DR index and how is it related to the price?
The DR index represents the strength of the site's link profile. A site with a low index requires more investment in building authority and acquiring external links.
Is the combination between organic and sponsored really necessary?
The combination is highly recommended because it allows you to take over a large screen area on Google, use the data from the sponsored for organic improvement and carry out remarketing to surfers.

title: The Future of SEO: Organic Search in 2025 and Beyond
content:
The digital world is in constant motion, and SEO is one of the areas most affected by these changes. For years, organic promotion was based on keywords, link building and quality content. But today, with the development of technology, and especially with the rise of artificial intelligence (AI), we are witnessing dramatic changes that are re-dictating the rules of the game. If you are a business owner, marketing manager or simply interested in the field, it is important to understand where the wind is blowing in order to stay relevant.

In this article, we'll take a look at what the future holds for SEO. We will begin with a brief overview of the past, move to the rapidly changing present, and end with a fascinating glimpse into the near and distant future. We will examine how artificial intelligence, voice search and other advanced technologies will affect organic promotion, and we will also offer you practical tools and tips for dealing with the new challenges and opportunities.

A word of transparencyThis article was created to provide you with knowledge and tools to help you make the best decisions for your business. Transparency is a top value for us. Therefore, it is important for us to point out that while the text is compiled with the help of advanced artificial intelligence technologies, it has been carefully checked and human edited by Adwrks 365's team of experts. The goal is to ensure that the information you receive is as accurate, relevant and useful as possible. Fun and educational reading!

What Once Was: The Road to Today's SEO

To understand the future, you need to know the past. In the early days of the Internet, Website promotion It was a relatively simple matter. Search engine algorithms were primitive, and promotion techniques were often manipulative. Promoters would use repeated keywords (Keyword Stuffing), build networks of spammy links and basically, try to "work" on the algorithm to climb to the top of the search results.

Google realized that this approach harms the quality of results for users and started working on more sophisticated algorithms. Updates like Panda, Penguin and Hummingbird changed the face of the field. Panda focused on quality content, Penguin fought spammy links, and Hummingbird moved to understanding search intent and not just the keywords themselves. Thus, promoters were required to move from "black techniques" (Black Hat SEO) to building websites with real value for users. The emphasis has shifted to quality keyword research, creating valuable content, and acquiring natural links.

Case study: the website "Luxury Watches" in 2010

The case of the "luxury watches" site illustrates how old SEO techniques have broken down.

In 2010, the site managed to climb to the top of the search results by using manipulative methods:

  • Keyword stuffing (Keyword Stuffing) – mechanical repetition of phrases like "luxury watches" in illegible text.
  • Artificial link building - Establishing private blog networks (PBNs) and spreading spammy links in forums.

These methods worked for a while, and the site enjoyed high traffic.

But in 2012, Google launched the "Penguin" update that penalized sites that used such tactics. The website of the luxury watches suffered a heavy penalty, deteriorated in the ranking of the search results, and had to spend a lot of effort to repair the damage.

The example shows that successful organic promotion today is not based on attempts to work on the algorithm, but on building authority and credibility over time.

The Changing Present: Today's SEO Revolution

Today we are already in the midst of a real revolution. Google has evolved from a search engine that only displays a list of links to a smart and complex system whose goal is to deeply understand the user's intent and provide him with direct, accurate and relevant answers - sometimes even before he enters the websites. This is the reason for changes such as the appearance of Featured Snippets, PAA (People Also Ask) and Knowledge Panels, and of course also for the launch of advanced technologies such as SGE (Search Generative Experience) and AI reviews of course.

At the heart of this change is a combination of machine learning (Machine Learning) and artificial intelligence (AI), which allow Google to understand broad topics and connections between them, far beyond individual keywords. That's why the focus of SEO has shifted to Search Intent and building "Topic Clusters" that prove expertise, authority and reliability (E-E-A-T), instead of creating partial and scattered articles.

At the same time, technical elements still significantly affect the rating - user experience (UX), Site speed, mobile compatibility and link quality. But here, too, a revolution has taken place: the emphasis is no longer on mass link building, but on quality links from reliable sites. In other words, today's SEO is a complex combination of technological innovation, high content quality and constant adaptation to user behavior.

The Future of SEO: Not Links, But Answers

From 2025 onwards, the emphasis in organic promotion is expected to shift from the "link economy" to the "answer economy". Google will become a system that focuses less on technical signals (such as keywords and links), and more on a deep understanding of the content and providing direct, immediate and relevant answers to the user.

1. The AI ​​Takes Command: Search Generative Experience (SGE)


What does this actually mean?

The biggest innovation from Google is the SGE (Search Generative Experience). Instead of displaying ten links, Google will use AI to create a ready summary of answers to the query - directly at the top of the results page (SERP). In many cases, the user won't even need to log in to the sites.

The implications for site promoters
  • Moving from information to insights: superficial or duplicated content will lose value. Only in-depth content with solutions and insights will succeed in standing out.
  • Optimized for SGE: using clear titles, logical structure, summaries and direct answers to frequently asked questions - so that the AI ​​can retrieve the information easily.
  • Dealing with a drop in clicks: Some of the answers will already be given in the SERP, so a strong call to action (CTA) will be required to motivate users to enter the site and dig deeper.

2. Voice search and conversational search


Why is this critical?

Voice assistants - Google Assistant, Siri, Alexa - have become an integral part of life. Instead of a short typing ("Italian restaurant Tel Aviv"), people ask full questions: "Hey Google, where is a good Italian restaurant in Tel Aviv?"

What needs to be changed?
  • Natural and conversational language: matching to full questions, not just short keywords.
  • Content in Q&A format: FAQ pages and structured answers within articles.
  • Local SEO: Regular updating of the Google Business Profile, because most voice searches are local ("near me").

3. Structured data (Schema Markup) - Google's secret language

Why is this important?

Schema Markup is code that helps search engines understand the site in depth. This gives context to each element: price, review, opening hours and more. If in the past it was mainly used for Rich Snippets, in the future it will be critical to be included in Google's AI answers.

How do you prepare?
  • Implementation of a relevant scheme: Product, Review, Recipe and more - according to the type of content.
  • Accuracy and up-to-dateness: Incorrect or outdated information harms credibility and ranking.

4. AI and content creation - challenge or opportunity?

what is happening today

AI tools like ChatGPT or Bard allow everyone to produce content quickly. The result: a flood of mediocre content, which forces Google to emphasize quality, uniqueness and authenticity.

How to stay relevant?
  1. AI as an assistant, not a replacement: Use tools to create drafts and ideas, but be sure to add editing, personal knowledge, and real insights.
  2. Focus on E-E-A-T:
  • Experience - real experience from the field.
  • Expertise - professional expertise.
  • Authoritativeness - recognized authority in the field.
  • Trustworthiness - reliability and transparency.

Highlight the writer, cite sources and add opinions to convey credibility.

Bottom line: SEO of 2025 and beyond will require less "dry technique" and more of a combination of quality content, deep understanding of users, smart use of AI and the ability to establish authority and trust over time.

What needs to be done to succeed in SEO in 2025?

The new landscape requires a holistic strategy that combines technical understanding, creativity, analytics and the ability to quickly adapt. Here are some key principles:

  • Stop thinking in terms of keywords, start thinking with user intent: Instead of asking "Which keyword should I write about?", ask "What problem of my audience can I solve?". The answer to this question will lead you to content that will receive a higher rating.
  • Become an authority on: Focus on building "content clusters" around key topics. Show Google that you are the expert in your field by creating comprehensive, accurate and useful content.
  • Invest in user experience (UX): Make sure your site is fast, mobile responsive and easy to navigate. If browsing the site is an unpleasant experience, the user will leave, and Google will punish you.
  • Optimization for AI Overviews: Answer frequently asked questions directly and concisely in the opening paragraphs or FAQ pages. Use structured data (Schema) to help Google understand your content type (recipe, review, FAQ, etc.).
  • Don't forget the basics: Despite all the changes, the basis remains the same. You still need to take care of proper technical SEO, quality link building and content distribution on social networks. The difference is that today everything has to be more focused, smarter and based on real value.

To conclude: SEO is not dead, it is changing

The thinking that SEO died with the development of AI is wrong. SEO isn't going away, it's just going to change. Instead of focusing on techniques, we will have to focus on strategic advice and building a holistic digital presence. The challenges are becoming more complex, but so are the opportunities.

As search engine algorithms become more sophisticated, so does the need for experts who understand this complexity. The strategy that will work in 2025 is one that focuses on creating real value, using the right tools and deeply understanding your audience.

Need help dealing with the future of SEO?

As you understand, the world of organic promotion has become more complex than ever. we are in We live and breathe these changes. Our team of experts consists of first-class SEO professionals who know the new Google algorithms, understand the psychology of search in the age of AI and use the most advanced tools to build customized promotion strategies for each business.

We don't believe in "tricks" or shortcuts. We work in full cooperation with our clients, and our goal is not only to bring traffic to the website, but to create a strong, authoritative and profitable digital presence over time. We will know how to produce quality content for you that is suitable for both voice search and AI Overviews, we will make sure that your site meets all of Google's technical requirements, and we will build a strong link profile for you that will place you at the top of your field.
